title: Minkä väristä: asking the colour of a substance
focus: For the colour of a substance, use minkä väristä. Minkä väristä maito on? — Maito on valkoista.
targetSkills: Minkä väristä: asking the colour of a substance
prerequisiteSkills: Minkä värisiä: asking about several things

exercises.prompt: Choose the question meaning “What colour is the milk?”
exercises.explanation: Singular refers to one person or one thing in these patterns. The partitive is a word form used here for an amount, an action's object, or a substance or group description. The genitive is a relationship form; in these question phrases minkä means of what or which. For the colour of a substance, use minkä väristä. Väristä is the singular partitive form in this question phrase. The substance subject stays in its basic form. The complete question means “What colour is the milk”.
requiredSkills: Minkä väristä: asking the colour of a substance
exercises.targetSkill: Minkä väristä: asking the colour of a substance

sentenceExplanation.pattern: question modifier (asks which item or group) + colour being asked about + subject (who or what this sentence is about) + verb (the action or state)

parts.role: question modifier (asks which item or group)
parts.formation: Minkä is the genitive form of mikä and remains unchanged in these descriptive question phrases.

parts.role: colour being asked about
parts.formation: Värinen changes -nen to -stä in singular partitive väristä.

parts.role: subject (who or what this sentence is about)
parts.formation: Maito stays in its basic form as the subject of a description.

parts.role: verb (the action or state)
parts.formation: Olla has the irregular singular third-person form on.
